incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: KV cache eviction rate spiked on cont-batching pools in us-west-2 at 14:04 UTC. Observed sustained paging and latency >10x for affected routes. Incident id: INC-20250304-89
sara: seeing huge KV eviction bursts, mem_used on g4s jumped to 94%. tailing logs show repeated full-kv-evict cycles.
devon: i think this tracks to a config drift — max_batch_tokens was bumped to 65536 in the autosync for a subset of pools last night. that will allow huge batches, increase KV working set, and force paging.
emily: confirmed. config change trace: `config-sync-job/2025-03-03T02:13 -> pool:cont-batch-usw2 -> max_batch_tokens: 65536 -> applied by automation`
tj: oncall handoff in 10. who's taking mitigation?
sara: i'm at keyboard, will try immediate rollback to previous safe values (max_batch_tokens=8192, max_num_seqs=16) and flip aggressive eviction back on. prepping a canary first.
devon: recommended immediate hotfix: set `max_batch_tokens=2048`, `max_num_seqs=8`, enable `kv.eviction.policy=aggressive`, and reduce `batch.timeout_ms` to 50 for the affected pools. lower values to force smaller batches and reduce KV pressure.
meera: assigning customer-impact assessment. initial query shows ~120 tenants experienced 5-10x tail latency and ~30 tenants saw 500s on generation endpoints between 14:04-14:22 UTC.
sara: applying canary patch to cont-batch-canary-usw2 now:
```
# apply patch to canary pool
redwoodctl pools update cont-batch-canary-usw2 --set max_batch_tokens=2048 --set max_num_seqs=8 --set kv.eviction=aggressive --set batch.timeout_ms=50
```
sara: canary looks stable after 60s, latency dropped from p95 3.2s -> 0.45s, eviction rate dropped 87%. rolling to remaining 6 pools in region.
emily: FYI, enabling aggressive eviction will increase token ejection but should reduce paging. watch for regens / coherence regressions.
devon: also patching autosync rule to block excessive max_batch_tokens > 16384 and add alert on kv_eviction_rate > 0.2.
tj: starting rolling hotfix now, will do sequential pool updates with 30s stabilization windows. leaving a manual gate before each.
meera: drafting initial customer note to affected customers, marking incident severity P2. will propose: brief summary, what we did, impacted window, mitigation status, ETA for postmortem.
alex: good. also add a follow-up task for config validation in CI to prevent autosync drift. create ticket and link to INC-20250304-89.
sara: hotfix roll completed at 14:18 UTC. observed normalization across metricset.
emily: post-roll check: p99 tokens/sec recovered, no new paging spikes.
devon: root cause (preliminary): automation pushed a too-large max_batch_tokens value allowing batch formation that exceeded KV cache design assumptions; combined with long `batch.timeout_ms` enabled huge, long-lived KV working sets causing page thrash and evictions. paging then increased IO latency causing higher request latencies and some 502/500s when memory pressure triggered OOM protections on a few nodes.
meera: customer impact summary: 14:04-14:18 UTC, degraded latency for generation & chat endpoints for ~120 tenants, 30 tenants had increased error rates. internal SLOs breached for 14m.
tj: transfer oncall to me at 14:25 UTC. i'm monitoring for 1h. leaving playbook notes and rollback steps in the incident doc.
sara: creating follow-up tasks: (1) revert autosync rule gap and add max cap; (2) add unit/integration tests for batch config vs kv memory estimation; (3) run dry-run simulation for cont-batching config changes; (4) schedule postmortem for tomorrow.
alex: please include the exact config diff and the patch command in the postmortem. also include customer-impact table and timeline.
meera: sent initial customer-facing note to support and key tenants at 14:30 UTC.
emily: thumbs up on mitigation. adding monitoring alerts: `kv_eviction_rate > 0.1 for 2m` and `batch_size_avg > 8192` to page oncall.
devon: logging todo: capture a full heap profile from one of the affected nodes and save to S3 under `s3://redwood-incident-dumps/INC-20250304-89/` before it ages out.
sara: heap profile uploaded. link: https://s3.redwood.internal/INC-20250304-89/heap-14-06.pb.gz
tj: handing off to meera for comms and alex for postmortem ownership. I'm out at 15:30 UTC for the next shift.
meera: acknowledged. will lead postmortem writeup, assign owners on tasks.
incident-bot: incident INC-20250304-89 acknowledged, severity: P2, status: mitigated -> monitoring, runbook link: https://redwood.internal/incidents/INC-20250304-89
meera: thanks everyone, will follow up with timeline + permanent mitigations. :thumbsup:
